key_insight: SkillBuffBench is designed to isolate how file-based Agent Skills and memory affect research-task performance across agent harnesses and models.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark could help engineers assess whether curated or automatically selected Skills improve scientific workflows enough to justify their cost and runtime.
method: Compare no Skill, a curated Skill and automatic invocation from an installed library.
Cross Skill access with memory off/on, four harnesses and multiple proprietary and open-weight models.
Use expert-contributed materials science and biology tasks, deterministic verifiers and paired task-level bootstrap uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Evaluation is in progress; the protocol reports task scores alongside cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time, but no performance results are available yet.
watch_item: Skill benefits remain unproven, and generalization will depend on task coverage and the installed Skill library.
paper_title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
